title: Bull's favourite New Orleans musicians
summary: Bull names his favourite musicians and drummers and describes sitting in at Dixieland Hall with Albert Burbank's group.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Who are your favourites, by the way?

Favourite musicians are Manuel Paul, for one, I don't know what you're just talking about. Captain Handy. George. Lewis. Jim. I like Lewis Nelson very much. I like Jim better. Dee Dee knocked me right out the night I heard Dee Dee. I've only heard him once, but that was tremendous. And Billy, of course, was good. She didn't play on the night, but she sang. And they did a couple of duets, which were really tremendous. I like Kid Thomas. I like Chester's artist very much. And Dre, I've only heard a couple of times, but he played well, I thought. Soi and Sammy Penn are the two best drummers, I think. I don't know who I like the best. I thought, you know, from records, I always thought Soi was better, but Sammy Penn is tremendous in person. Who else is there? Albert Burbank I liked very much. I played one set with him around the Dixieland Hall. I like him. What band was he playing with at Dixieland Hall? Frog Joseph. And I think it was Albert French's band, but Albert French wasn't there.

No, no. It was Albert Burbank, Jack Willis, Frog Joseph. Jeanette Kimball played piano. She's good, too. And some fellow called Frank on bass. Frank's somebody or other on bass. Fields, Frank Fields. And Louis Barberin on drums. But who else is there? Well, I like Frank Moyet very much, the piano player. And Charlie Hamilton's also a good pianist. Who else is there? I liked what little he did of Earl Humphrey over the river. Last Saturday he played with the Thomas band over the river at this dance. And he has a bit of a problem with his drinking, I think. And he's out of practice, but he did a few things which were really tremendous.
